title: Radio: Stockton Dock — Trailer HT-5512 Reefer Fault, Door 7

lines.text: Logistics, Stockton dock. The reefer on trailer HT-5512 at dock door 7 is throwing alarm code RA SENSOR FAULT. The display keeps jumping between 36 and 47 degrees.
It's the Harvest Table load, baby spinach, lot PF1-27284-L3-A, packed yesterday. Supposed to pull out at 06:45. I put a probe in a case up in the nose and it reads 37 degrees.
So, do I hold it, swap trailers, or is this part of the thing everybody's being called about? Stockton dock, standing by.

fields.voiceStyle: Male, mid-30s, practical and a little rushed, shouting slightly over reefer units and forklifts on a busy early-morning dock

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. The lot is from line L3, packed October 11, and the probe reads 37°F, so it is a sensor fault, not a temperature excursion, and it is outside the five-lot recall scope. The Director of Logistics should send it back to the Stockton dock lead to swap the trailer or call a reefer tech under normal procedure, keep the load cold, and go straight back to the hold. Note it if anyone adds this lot to the hold or lets it pull the team away from the hold.

citations.documentTitle: PFC-OPS-02: Plant, Distribution Network and Cold Chain
citations.quote: Pinecrest uses two truckload carriers (Cascade Reefer Lines and Sonoran Cold Freight, both fictional) with refrigerated trailers that carry a temperature recorder; a reefer trailer carries 22 pallets

citations.headingPath: PPDNCC › 7. Systems and people at the DC
citations.quote: Each DC has a WMS, a labeling station and a records clerk on the day shift; the night shift of 12 people handles receiving. Radio scanners read the lot code on the case label. DC managers send a hold

citations.documentTitle: PFC-FS-01: Product Hold, Trace and Recall Plan
citations.quote: - A lot is a production lot by line, shift and date. Any lot made on the same line within 24 hours after a positive result on that line, before sanitation was verified, is in scope. Raw material lots
